items.title: Show HN: Klistra – Make launch videos and product demos, all in one AI studio
items.summary: I built Klistra: describe your video idea and add your logo, photos or other assets, Klistra designs and animates a video for you, exported for every screen size, with fonts, media and logos kept exact. Deterministic renders make features exact and isolated, allowing for superior control and iteration compared to diffusion models. Here's a short demo render where I made an ad for Klistra itself: https://app.klistra.ai/s/4EQoWCe37SkYz5nThgegzw As a solo dev with a lot of projects going on, I found myself needing to make short promos or explainer videos. Not being familiar with animation software, I had the idea to use Claude to code up those videos and export them as video files. In the process of creating these clips I stumbled into a bunch of bugs and setup needed to make it work reliably. The list of features I wanted for better control and feedback kept growing and I needed to sign up for a bunch of services to get music, voiceovers and other media into my project. I couldn't find an existing service that had everything I wanted. Seeing these hurdles and that the technology was only easily accessible to people already confident with coding agents, I started working on Klistra, and a couple of months later I'm turning it into a service so you all can use it too. The goal with Klistra was to include everything I missed in the manual workflow in an easy-to-use service with a nice UI, so people could focus on what they wanted the video to look like, not setting up the framework behind it. Klistra includes precise timeline control, media generation, built-in support to make animations match the rhythm of the background music, word extraction from voiceovers or songs, a dedicated iteration / feedback tool, website import and much more. Something I knew I needed to get right was making it easy to iterate on small features of the video with precise control of what was being built. I designed Klistra so you first create a specification where you define scenes in detail, describe what you want shown and when, reference media or timestamps in-line, freely drag the timeline around and preview the result before letting a builder agent create the video. If you want to change something, the specification changes and the builder agent gets a diff of what changed. There is also a planner agent built into Klistra that helps create and edit the specification for you (which is what I use the most), while letting you turn to manual fine-tuning when needed. Don't think of this as a replacement for diffusion models, if you want photorealistic images or videos they clearly do a better job. Klistra really shines when you need motion design and precise control, exact text with your fonts, media such as logos or voiceovers, animated UI that matches your apps and so on. Klistra does have built-in integrations for generating media from diffusion models, and combining the two technologies usually gets the best results. Everything that costs money to run on Klistra, from machines to AI tokens, is paid for with credits included in a subscription or bought via one-time packs (Pro starts at $25/mo ($20 billed yearly) and packs at $12). Being a solo dev without funding, the budget wouldn't allow for a free tier with enough monthly credits for a real project. I instead decided to give the first 200 of you who sign up 350 free credits, enough for a simple video (the advanced tutorial used around 250 credits). There is also a Claude Code integration in paid subscriptions, where your agent can act as a planner, convenient if you already have a project built with Claude that has all the context and you need an explainer, ad or social post. It also reduces credit spending if you're a heavy planner user. - Tutorial, mostly using the planner: https://klistra.ai/docs/basic - Advanced features and manual control: https://klistra.ai/docs/advanced - More demos: https://klistra.ai/ Happy to hear what you think!

items.title: Show HN: Stop applying to jobs using AI-generated resume
items.summary: When LLMs hands you a resume or pdf it carry markers of how it was made, including the source. You can't see them on the page but applicant tracking systems can read it. So recruiters are flagging such profiles and rejecting them entirely. I had tested this across 40+ AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, etc) to produce a resume and every single file carried a marker. To solve this problem. I had built a free tool to show what your file says and gives you a cleaned version: - Drop your resume and get a cleaned copy - Free, no account. What it doesn't do: it won't rewrite your resume or make AI-sounding wording more human. It only deals with what's hidden in the file. It's a simple tool, but it feels absolutely necessary now as more people are using AI for generating their entire resume or even editing them. I am the developer, happy to answer any questions.

items.title: Show HN: Musset, open-source Scrivener alternative with an AI that never writes
items.summary: I’m writing my first novel and could not find an app that fit my workflow: quiet like iA Writer, organized like Scrivener, and with AI so I can discuss my book while I write it. It allows me to feel less “alone” and have a sounding board while I write. - A book is a folder of plain Markdown files. Musset commits to a git repo, tracks versions and drafts without you having to know git. - Revisions are CriticMarkup inside the text. It manages docx revisions too, so your editor can edit a Word doc and you import their comments. - PDFs are typeset using Typst, embedded in the app, following each language’s typographic rules. - Spelling and grammar are checked using LanguageTool, also embedded. - Mac/Word, WordStar, vi and Emacs keyboard modes. The AI is optional and uses your Codex or Claude Code CLI. It comments, leaves margin notes, and checks continuity and your chapters against your style rules. It’s GPL-3.0 and free during the beta. When or if it reaches 1.0, if there is sufficient interest, the idea is to make it a small one-time payment ($9.90). There is a paid sync service (git hosting) that lets you share a book with beta readers and editors. Download: https://musset.app I’d love to have some feedback!

items.title: Preview seed fixture (rolling)
items.summary: Rolling, fully SYNTHETIC preview-database seed fixture baked from dev@10ddacffc54f (migration head: 20261120120000_add_onboarding_wizard_writer). Preview environments restore fixture.dump.gz (custom-format, gzipped, platform schema only, including _prisma_migrations) BEFORE running a PR's own migrations, so schema changes run against populated tables. RESTORE: apply restore-preamble.sql to the target database first (it creates the platform schema and installs the vector + pg_trgm extensions into it, which pg_dump --schema=platform omits), then run 'gunzip -c fixture.dump.gz | pg_restore -d --no-owner' WITHOUT --exit-on-error (the dump's own CREATE SCHEMA collides benignly with the preamble's). SECURITY INVARIANT: this bake holds no cloud credentials and has no read path to any real database — it runs entirely against a throwaway Postgres container and contains only synthetic rows (Faker-generated, plus the hand-written preview marketplace) and the already-public marketplace agent exports checked into autogpt_platform/backend/agents/. This asset is regenerated on every eligible dev push and weekly; treat it as disposable.
